claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 ceramic is the initial material state.
Adding a sintering aid through a liquid-phase method can lower the required preparation temperature of ZrB2.
The intervention can reduce holes and defects in ZrB2 ceramic.
Reducing holes and defects through the intervention will improve structural integrity.
A preparation-temperature range of 1800-2200 °C is relevant to the proposed intervention.
A service-temperature range of 1000-1500 °C is relevant to the proposed material.
The intervention will reduce porosity and improve densification.
The sintering aid facilitates liquid-phase sintering.
Liquid-phase sintering enhances particle rearrangement and densification.
Enhanced particle rearrangement and densification reduce the formation of holes and defects.
The modified ZrB2 will have greater strength than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
The modified ZrB2 will have lower porosity than conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed preparation boundary is below 2300 °C.
The intended service boundary includes prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
A controlled comparison of ZrB2 made with and without the sintering aid can test the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly framed as single-phase ZrB2, but adding an unspecified sintering aid through a liquid phase may introduce a residual secondary phase; the hypothesis does not state how single-phase status will be retained or verified.
